description:
My name is Sara

I’m excited to introduce our team and our project, “Abandoned, But Not Forgotten” — a storytelling initiative exploring the history of NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars.

As someone interested in technology, coding, artificial intelligence, and space exploration.

Through this project, our team aims to bring these forgotten pieces of space exploration back into the spotlight, exploring their history, scientific purpose, and the legacy they leave behind.
summary:
Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive digital archive that preserves the stories of space missions that have ended. Robotic explorers like rovers, telescopes and landers make remarkable discoveries, but once they fall silent, their achievements are scattered across reports, articles and databases and gradually fade from public memory.

We built a website where each mission has its own page with an introduction, a narrative story, major discoveries, a historical timeline, technical specifications and a gallery of authentic NASA imagery. Our archive features missions including Kepler, Apollo 11 and the Perseverance rover.

The project addresses the challenge by turning technical mission data into accessible, engaging storytelling. It is important because it keeps the history of space exploration alive, makes scientific information understandable to students and the public, and inspires curiosity about astronomy and technology. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, it is lightweight, easy to expand, and ready to grow with more missions. Every mission deserves to be remembered, even after its journey ends.
details: Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive, web-based archive dedicated to documenting historic space exploration missions, particularly those involving the Moon and Mars. The project explores the stories behind historic missions, spacecraft, and technologies by presenting mission histories, historical timelines, engineering details, technical specifications, and scientific discoveries through dedicated sections. Its main objective is to preserve the legacy of space exploration and make its history more accessible, educational, and engaging for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. By highlighting the achievements and scientific contributions of missions that are often overlooked, the platform encourages visitors to discover the importance of spacecraft technology and understand how past discoveries continue to shape our knowledge of the universe. What makes the project creative is its combination of historical documentation and digital storytelling. Rather than presenting information as ordinary text, it uses cinematic visual design, interactive navigation, mission timelines, engineering details, and organized content to create an engaging experience. The project was developed using HTML5 to structure the website, CSS3 for styling, layouts, animations, and responsive design, and JavaScript for interactive functionality. Visual Studio Code was used for code development, while web browsers were used for testing and debugging. Research was conducted using NASA mission archives, official documentation, and educational resources. The website was developed using standard computer hardware without requiring specialized equipment. Throughout development, our team considered several important factors, including historical and scientific accuracy, reliable documentation, user-friendly navigation, responsive design across different devices, clear presentation of complex technical information, visual storytelling, accessibility, and the preservation of overlooked space missions. Ultimately, our goal is to inspire future generations to explore space science, astronomy, and aerospace engineering while reminding them that even when a spacecraft’s mission ends, its discoveries and contributions remain valuable. A mission may end, but its legacy is never abandoned.
